A.name: Snap
A.blurb: Keep every whole size Sotto already leans on and snap the halves and one-offs to the nearest. A half-pixel size goes down to the step below, except under 12 px, where it goes up.

type.use: Transcript, composer, journal entries, settings labels
Dialog titles, section intros, request prompts
Figures in a narrow room, sub-titles

Sidebar and menu rows, icon buttons

B.name: Six steps
B.blurb: The issue’s six-step ramp, named with the iPhone’s six roles. Nothing is smaller than 12 px. Reading text and settings labels drop from 15 to 14; radii keep four steps, so rows and dialogs lose some roundness.

type.use: Sidebar rows, fields, transcript, composer, settings labels

radius.use: Cards, the composer and dialogs (today’s lg)

C.name: Fluent
C.blurb: Windows’ own ramp and corners: Caption 12, Body 14, Body Large 18, Subtitle 20, Title 28; 4 px for controls and rows, 8 px for cards and overlays. Each size goes to the role it plays, so 13 px interface text becomes Body 14 and 15 px reading text becomes Body 14 too. At 820 × 560 it costs little room (the Settings card grows 11 px, the dialog 13 px); what it costs is hierarchy and the soft corners.

type.use: Body and Body Strong: all interface and reading text
Body Large: dialog titles, section intros
Title: room titles and large figures

radius.use: Cards, the composer, menus and dialogs
